## HIGH-priority finding details

### H-1: SSO/OIDC admin auth entirely undocumented  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: `environment-variables.mdx` documented only `ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE`, claiming the UI is "disabled entirely" without it.
- **Source**: `src/index.ts:117-139` and `src/oauth/providers.ts:43-59` — Google/Microsoft SSO is the preferred path; `ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE` is a deprecated fallback. The UI is disabled only when *neither* is set.
- **Edit**: Added a new "Admin UI authentication" subsection with `OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/TENANT`, and `OAUTH_ALLOWED_DOMAINS/EMAILS`; marked `ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE` deprecated.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-2: `/ai-implement` architecture stale in environment-variables.mdx  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`'s description only mentioned review-feedback follow-ups; `GAP_FILL_TRIGGER_SECRET` explicitly claimed `/ai-implement` "runs entirely inside `comment-trigger.yml`... never calls the orchestrator"; the target-repo secrets tab and legacy run-cap variables were presented as current, unqualified guidance.
- **Source**: `src/index.ts:2403-2409` — the webhook endpoint (gated on `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) now handles `issue_comment` events directly; `src/gap-fill-trigger.ts:137-142` — the old comment-trigger dispatch path is dead code.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` paragraph to list both capabilities it gates; rewrote the `GAP_FILL_TRIGGER_SECRET` accordion; dropped `comment-trigger.yml` from the secrets-tab intro; added a Warning to "Gap-fill run caps" and marked `AI_IMPLEMENT_SKILLS_REPO` deprecated, both scoped to legacy pre-migration repos.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-3: `preflight` step description inverted  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: `custom-steps.mdx` described `preflight` as pre-implementation workspace/tool validation that runs before Claude starts.
- **Source**: `src/pipeline/steps/preflight.ts:18-83` runs `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` **after** the feedback loop, gated on review approval; pipeline order in `pipelines/autonomous.yml:16-17` confirms this.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the accordion to describe the actual post-implementation quality-gate behavior.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-4: `push` step skip condition backwards  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: Claimed `push` is "automatically skipped when the feedback-loop did not approve the diff."
- **Source**: `src/pipeline/pipeline-loader.ts:151-163` skips `push` only on gap-fill runs (existing PR number); on an unapproved diff it still runs and opens a **draft PR** (`src/pipeline/steps/push.ts:172-178`).
- **Edit**: Corrected the skip condition and added the draft-PR behavior so a fork overriding this step doesn't break the draft-PR fallback.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-5: Admin UI docs omit SSO auth  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: `admin-ui.mdx` stated the UI "is protected by the `ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE` environment variable" with no mention of SSO; the Authentication/API-reference section only documented the access-code token exchange.
- **Source**: `src/index.ts:2581-2628` mounts `/api/auth/providers`, `/api/auth/:provider/start|callback`, `/api/auth/logout`; the UI is disabled only when neither SSO nor the access code is configured.
- **Edit**: Updated the intro line, added a note that SSO has no scriptable token exchange, and added the four SSO routes to the endpoint reference table.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-6: Run-cap fields wrongly claimed to be in the creation stepper  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: Claimed the New Project stepper's Capacity step exposes `maxTurns`/`maxIterations`/`maxJobMinutes`, with a full table under the stepper walkthrough.
- **Source**: `src/admin-ui/stepper.ts:210-225` — the stepper's Capacity step contains only "Max parallel AI issues"; the three caps exist solely in the separate Edit dialog (`src/admin-ui/pages/projects.ts:134-136`). This also contradicts `team-repo-mappings.mdx`, which already correctly documents these as edit-only.
- **Edit**: Removed the false stepper table, replaced with a Tip pointing to the Edit dialog and defaults.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-7: `profilesFieldOverride` undocumented; override-field count wrong  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: `team-repo-mappings.mdx`'s `ticketingConfig` JSON example and prose listed only `statusFieldOverride`/`repoFieldOverride`, saying "the two ...Override fields."
- **Source**: `src/providers/ticketing-config.ts:17-19` defines a third field, `profilesFieldOverride`, wired to the "AI-Implement Profiles" multi-select field and admin UI dropdown (`src/admin-ui/pages/projects.ts:320,645-652`).
- **Edit**: Added `profilesFieldOverride` to the JSON example and prose (now "the three"), plus a Note on what the Profiles field does.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-8: `sessionMode` has no effect under default execution mode  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: Described `interactive`/`hybrid` unconditionally, with no execution-mode caveat.
- **Source**: `src/fly-machines.ts:406,444` and `src/local-docker.ts:62` set `SESSION_MODE` only for Fly/local Docker; the GitHub Actions dispatch path (`src/github.ts`) never forwards it, and `github-actions` is the default `executionMode`.
- **Edit**: Added a Warning that `sessionMode` only takes effect under `executionMode: fly-machines`.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-9: Jira blocking-semantics claim contradicts source  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: Stated "Unlike Linear, Jira has no built-in blocking semantics here."
- **Source**: `src/providers/jira.ts:125-150,252-255` implements an equivalent "Blocks" link-based skip, explicitly commented as mirroring Linear's behavior.
- **Edit**: Replaced the Warning with a Note describing the actual Blocks-link gating and the link-type-rename caveat.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-10: Sync-workflows Tip backwards  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: Told readers the `/ai-implement` trigger "requires `comment-trigger.yml`" and to run **Sync workflows** to get it if missing.
- **Source**: `src/workflow-sync.ts:27-32` — sync unconditionally **removes** `comment-trigger.yml`; the trigger is now handled by the orchestrator's own webhook.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the Tip to describe the webhook requirement and clarify that Sync workflows removes the old file. The same underlying architecture fix was applied to `github-app.mdx` (webhook now required, not optional, for `/ai-implement`), `troubleshooting.mdx` (fixed a troubleshooting step that told readers to install a file that gets removed), `quickstart.mdx`, `how-it-works.mdx`, and `gap-analysis.mdx` (all described `/ai-implement` gap-fill as running through `comment-trigger.yml`).
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-11: Concurrency cap omits planning-phase issues  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: "controls how many issues... can have in flight (`AI-Working` in Linear, or `Implementing` in Jira)."
- **Source**: `src/providers/linear.ts:276-278` and `src/providers/jira.ts:280-282` both also count planning-phase issues (`AI-Planning`/`Planning`) against the same cap.
- **Edit**: Added a Note clarifying both phases occupy a slot.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-12: Monitor-detected failures revert Jira status silently  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: Claimed `Implementation Failed`/`Planning Failed` are set "when the run errors."
- **Source**: This is only true for runner-self-reported failures (`src/providers/jira.ts:556-569`). Orchestrator-detected failures (timeouts, killed jobs, orphaned machines — `src/index.ts:1737,1849,1884,1946`) instead revert the status to `Plan Approved` (`src/providers/jira.ts:571-573`), never surfacing a `*Failed` status.
- **Edit**: Added a Note explaining the distinction and pointing readers to the dispatch log/sessions panel for orchestrator-detected failures.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-13: Sync PR file list wrong  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: `target-repo.mdx` listed `comment-trigger.yml` among files the sync PR adds.
- **Source**: `src/workflow-sync.ts:27-32,438-444` — sync removes this file unconditionally.
- **Edit**: Dropped it from the file list; added a Note explaining removal is expected for repos that have it from before.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

### H-14: `comment-trigger.yml` documented as an active synced file  (1/1 runs)
- **Docs**: `workflow-templates.mdx` described three workflow files installed by sync, including a `comment-trigger.yml` section.
- **Source**: Same evidence as H-10/H-13 — `src/workflow-sync.ts:27-32`.
- **Edit**: Changed "three" to "two"; replaced the `comment-trigger.yml` section with one describing the webhook-based trigger and a Note about legacy file removal.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only run).

## Synthesis decisions log (audit-trail for reviewers)

Only `run-1/audit-report.md` exists among the three planned matrix jobs. `run-2/` and `run-3/`
directories are present with edited `.mdx` files under `latest/`, but neither contains an
`audit-report.md`. Without a report, there is no finding title, source citation, or priority call
to attribute those edits to — using them would mean guessing at what drift they address, which
risks silently introducing or reprioritizing findings the "no fabrication" rule forbids. Per Step
d ("if only one run produced an edit, use that one"), every HIGH finding below has exactly one
usable candidate (run-1's), so no edit-selection comparison was needed. Because only one run's
report was available, every finding's recurrence is 1/1 and no dedup or priority-conflict
resolution was necessary — the "union" here is a single input set reformatted into the synthesis
shape, not a merge across runs.

### H-1 through H-14
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH (all fourteen)
- **Dedup reasoning:** N/A — only one run's report was available; no cross-run duplicates to resolve.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 1 (the only candidate for every affected docs file).

### M-1 through M-15
- **Present in:** Run 1 MEDIUM (all fifteen)
- **Dedup reasoning:** N/A — only one run's report was available.

### Incompleteness notes

Missing runs (no `audit-report.md`): run-2, run-3. Both left partial artifacts:

- `audit-runs/run-2/latest/` contains 13 edited `.mdx` files (including two files run-1 never
  touched: `latest/customize/runner-image.mdx`, `latest/setup/deploy.mdx`), but no
  `audit-report.md`.
- `audit-runs/run-3/latest/` contains 19 edited `.mdx` files (including files run-1 never touched:
  `latest/customize/workflow-md.mdx`, `latest/introduction.mdx`, `latest/providers/anthropic.mdx`,
  `latest/providers/aws-bedrock.mdx`, `latest/reference/error-codes.mdx`,
  `latest/setup/deploy.mdx`, `latest/skills/introduction.mdx`), but no `audit-report.md`.

This pattern (edited files present, report absent) suggests each matrix job wrote its docs edits
but failed or was cut off before writing its report — the reverse order from what a crash early in
the run would produce. Actual failure details live in the matrix jobs' logs in the Actions UI, not
recoverable from the artifacts synthesized here. Because those two runs' underlying findings are
unknown, their edits were **not** used as alternate candidates for any HIGH finding above, even
where they touch the same docs file as a run-1 edit (e.g. both touch
`latest/reference/admin-ui.mdx`) — doing so would risk conflating a different, unreported drift
with a run-1 finding it doesn't actually match.
